t:
(a) Immigration and Nationality Act.—Section 286(i) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1356(i)) is amended by striking the last sentence and inserting the following: “Reimbursements under this subsection may be collected in advance of the provision of such immigration inspection services. Notwithstanding subsection (h)(1)(B), and only to the extent provided in appropriations Acts, any amounts collected under this subsection shall be credited as offsetting collections to the currently applicable appropriation, account, or fund of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, remain available until expended, and be available for the purposes for which such appropriation, account, or fund is authorized to be used.”. 
    (b) Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002.—Section 10412(b) of the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002 (7 U.S.C. 8311(b)) is amended to read as follows:“(b) Funds Collected for Preclearance.—Funds collected for preclearance activities—“(1) may be collected in advance of the provision of such activities;“(2) shall be credited as offsetting collections to the currently applicable appropriation, account, or fund of U.S. Customs and Border Protection;“(3) shall remain available until expended;“(4) shall be available for the purposes for which such appropriation, account, or fund is authorized to be used; and“(5) may be collected and shall be available only to the extent provided in appropriations Acts.”.

fable.w: This section only amends how reimbursements and preclearance funds are collected, credited, and made available to U.S. Customs and Border Protection. The tempting reading is that reimbursements paid by outside parties, or the reference to appropriations Acts, imply outside involvement, but paying fees is not consultation and Congress is inside the federal government. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking, or right to sue appears.
fable.s: any amounts collected under this subsection shall be credited as offsetting collections to the currently applicable appropriation, account, or fund of U.S. Customs and Border Protection

opus.w: This section only covers money. It lets fees and reimbursements for inspection and preclearance services be collected in advance, credited to U.S. Customs and Border Protection accounts, and spent. The tempting reading is that outside parties paying reimbursements are taking part, but paying for a service doesn't involve anyone outside the federal government in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
opus.s: Reimbursements under this subsection may be collected in advance of the provision of such immigration inspection services.

qwen_chat.w: This section deals exclusively with the accounting and appropriation of funds collected for preclearance activities. It specifies that funds are credited to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (a federal agency) and are subject to appropriations Acts (Congress, which is inside the federal government). There is no requirement or recommendation for consultation, coordination, or participation with any outside parties (such as states, tribes, the public, or foreign governments) in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_chat.s: Funds collected for preclearance activities—“(1) may be collected in advance of the provision of such activities;“(2) shall be credited as offsetting collections to the currently applicable appropriation, account, or fund of U.S. Customs and Border Protection;“(3) shall remain available until expended;“(4) shall be available for the purposes for which such appropriation, account, or fund is authorized to be used; and“(5) may be collected and shall be available only to the extent provided in appropriations Acts.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "preclearance activities" involve coordination with foreign governments or local entities, implying participation. However, the text itself only describes the financial handling of funds collected for these activities (offsetting collections, availability until expended). It does not describe the process of consultation or coordination with outside parties. The actors mentioned are U.S. Customs and Border Protection (federal) and Congress (via appropriations Acts, which is inside the government). There is no mention of consulting with states, tribes, the public, or foreign entities in this specific section.
